A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, Figure 1, references, and complete Appendices A and B are readable and can be matched despite additions and repagination.

before.justification: Section 3 reports the authors' original analysis of 57 papers, including percentages of recurring limitations. Appendix A supplies per-paper classifications and Appendix B the category key.

after.justification: v2 retains the original 57-paper analysis, its aggregate percentages, and the per-paper classifications in the appendices. These qualify as original data-analysis results despite the position-paper framing.

M1.justification: Both versions present the same sociocultural framework and localization agenda. The added explanations and recommendations introduce no algorithm, model component, training objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: The analyzed corpus remains the same 57 papers in Appendix A. Newly cited studies and illustrative examples support discussion; they do not introduce datasets or tasks actually evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed system against baselines. The added references are conceptual support, with no change to an evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Both versions describe the same illustrative survey of 57 papers from 2022–2024, analyzing self-stated limitations with the same category key. No evaluation protocol, sample size, metric, or experimental setting changes.

E4.justification: The existing culture-from-text case study and interaction examples are retained. Additions to Section 5 explain their interpretation and cite related research; no new empirical case study, ablation, robustness test, or error analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report descriptive survey percentages without uncertainty estimates, significance tests, repeated-run information, or annotation-reliability statistics. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Section 3 retains the same percentages: coverage 40%, nationality proxies 36%, dynamicity 12%, proxy limitations 37%, coarseness 28%, and stereotypes 14%. Appendix A retains the same per-paper limitation assignments, with no added original results.

T1.justification: The sociocultural framework remains conceptual. Neither version supplies mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs; the added analogies and qualifications do not introduce formal mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph, and conclusion retain the same central claims about the theoretical gap, stereotypes learned from cultural discourse, and localization as a useful framing. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly explains that in-group discourse can also express stereotypes and that contextual metadata can reveal first-order social meaning. Sections 4.2 and 6.2 clarify the identity–culture relationship and resource/design tradeoffs. The stated limitations in Section 8 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The surveyed-paper list and category definitions retain the same reproducibility information. No implementation instructions, annotation procedures, hardware details, hyperparameters, or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused connections to self-stereotyping research, computational sociolinguistics, and user-centered/participatory design, including Coffman (2014), Grieve et al. (2019), and Caselli et al. (2021). The central positioning around Bucholtz and Hall remains unchanged; other reference changes largely update bibliographic information.

P1.justification: v2 expands selected passages in Sections 4.2, 5, and 6.2, moves and explains the stereotype definition, makes wording and bibliography edits, and adds acknowledgments. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and the appendix table formats remain unchanged. Appendix A now starts on a separate page instead of sharing one with references, and the survey table and category key are repaginated, with the key continuing onto the final page.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the central argument more precise by explaining self-stereotyping and explicitly acknowledging computational access to first-order social meaning through metadata (Section 5.1). The resource discussion and design references make the localization guidance more concrete (Section 6.2). These are useful, limited improvements to a paper whose core claims and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
